name: California

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt, but carbonated drinks (soda, sparkling water) are taxed at the full rate, which is not counted here.

Quick-service restaurants: cold food sold to go (unless the seller meets the 80-80 rule) and hot coffee, tea and bakery goods sold to go for a separate price are exempt, so the full rate overstates the tax on some quick-service sales.
Household supplies: children's diapers are exempt (since 2020, with no end date), which is not taken out here.
Personal care products: menstrual products are exempt (since 2020, with no end date), which is not taken out here.
Barber and beauty services, laundry and dry cleaning, and auto repair labor: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Gasoline: 2.25% sales tax plus district taxes, July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 (diesel 13%); the district taxes are counted on top of the 2.25%. The per-gallon excise tax, left out here, rose from 61.2 to 63.4 cents on July 1, 2026; a March 2026 bill to suspend it died in committee (reported).
The 7.25% statewide rate includes 1.25% for local governments.

California cities and counties levy no local taxes on restaurant meals: state law allows local sales taxes only under the Bradley-Burns and district (transactions and use) tax laws, which are in the rates here.

Nicotine e-cigarettes also carry the 12.5% California Electronic Cigarette Excise Tax on the retail price, which isn't counted here: it falls only on e-cigarettes, and their share of tobacco sales can't be computed from official figures alone. The tax brought in $36.8 million in fiscal 2024-25 (about $295 million of taxable sales), against 371 million packs of cigarettes, but the CDTFA publishes no retail price for those packs; at $9 to $10 a pack, e-cigarettes would be about 7% to 8% of the two together (CDTFA Tables 30A and 30B).

Hotel stays carry no state tax; cities and counties levy their own transient occupancy taxes (Los Angeles 14%; San Francisco 14% plus a 2% to 2.25% tourism district assessment; San Diego 11.75% to 13.75% by zone since May 1, 2025), which are not counted here (city finance pages).
Tobacco is assumed taxed at the general rate (excise taxes left out); not verified state by state.
